 Judgment

1. This appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C. is filed challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 05.05.2018 passed by the District and Sessions Judge at Raichur in S.C.No.05/2015, by which, the appellants-accused have been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 323, 506, 376(D) R/w Section 34 of IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) R/w Section 34 of IPC; to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 363 R/w Section 34 of IPC; to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- and Rs.3,000/- each for the offences punishable under Sections 323 and 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC respectively.
2.

sentences.text:
The case of the prosecution in brief is as follows:
On 05.09.2014 at about 1.30 p.m., when the victim was waiting for the bus in the bus stop at Barma Camp, accused No.1 took her in an auto rickshaw and went to Araginamara NC: 2023:KHC-K:1412 Camp bus stop and stopped the auto rickshaw wherein accused Nos.2 and 3 boarded the auto rickshaw and drove the same towards Potanal side and closed the doors of the auto rickshaw in order to seduce the complainant to have intercourse and after kidnapping her, when she asked the accused as to where they are taking her instead of proceeding towards Sindhanur, the accused criminally intimated her by threatening her. Accused No.1 by threatening her with a dire consequences, accused No.2 by showing knife, accused No.1 by twisting her right side wrist and accused No.3 by slapping on her cheek, took her to a baron land bearing Sy. No.167/3 situated on the outskirts of Potanal village and after Shri. Tillai Nadan And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117043159/
2 dragging her had forcible sexual intercourse one after another.
3.

sentences.text: The learned Sessions Judge, after framing the charge for the aforesaid offences, read over and explained the same to the accused, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tired.
4. The prosecution to prove its case, examined PW.1 to PW.21 and exhibited the documents at Exs.P1 to P38 and marked material objects at MOs.1 and 2.

After conclusion of the evidence of the prosecution, the incriminating circumstances adduced by the prosecution was put to the accused, to which, the accused denied and marked documents at Exs.D1 and D2.
5.

The learned Sessions Judge, after examining the evidence on record and after framing the points for consideration, recorded a finding that the prosecution has NC: 2023:KHC-K:1412 established the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and passed the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants- accused and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
7.
Admittedly, there are no eyewitnesses to the incident.
The prosecution to prove its case relied on the statement of the victim and also the medical opinion and the author of the medical opinion, and the spot panchanama.
8. PW.2-victim in her examination-in-chief has reiterated the averments made in the First Information Report and supported the case of the prosecution.

In the cross- examination, she has denied the suggestion that she has not stated before the police that the accused closed the doors of the auto and the auto which was shown to her has no doors on two sides.

In the cross-examination,
the place of occurrence was wrongly described due to shock, the portion of which is marked as Ex.P1.
She has further stated that there was a traffic on the road and also movement of people on the date of incident.
There are minor discrepancies and omissions in the statement of the victim with regard to the place of occurrence.
Since there were no eyewitnesses to the incident, the prosecution has to establish the guilt of the accused on the basis of the corroborative material in the form of medical opinion.
PW.13 is the author of the wound certificate and in her evidence she has deposed on oath that, on examination there were no injuries over the external generatic.
Small abrasions 3-4 over the right arm.
Cx-vagina heavy hymen old rupture.

Presence of seminal stains was not detected on articles 1 to 26 and presence of spermatozoa was not detected on articles 3 and 5 and on local examination there was no recent signs of sexual intercourse and FSL report was negative for seminal stain estimation.

10. Perusal of the medical evidence establishes that there was no recent forcible sexual intercourse on the victim and the rupture of hymen was old, though the case of the prosecution is that three Shri. Tillai Nadan And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117043159/
3 accused persons raped the victim one after another.

sentences.text: 11. The sketch map at Ex.P18 indicates that the incident had taken place 100 mtrs. from the State Highway and it was a baron land with no standing crops.
The State Highway is busy with vehicles and movement of people during the afternoon hours at 1.30 p.m.

Except the statement of the victim that she was sexually assaulted by the accused herein, the prosecution has not produced any corroborative evidence to substantiate that the accused herein had forcible sexual intercourse.

12. On perusal of the evidence on record, especially the wound certificate at Ex.P14 and the evidence of the doctor namely, PW.13, the prosecution has failed to establish that the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1412 accused herein had forcible sexual intercourse.

The learned Sessions Judge has committed an error in passing the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence solely based on the testimony of the victim and also wrongly presumed that the victim might have washed her vagina and also the clothes before she was examined by the doctor, when there is no statement of the victim to that effect.
The approach of the learned Sessions Judge in coming to such a conclusion is erroneous and is not based on any evidence on record.

Hence, the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence insofar as relates to convicting the appellants-accused for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) R/w Section 34 of IPC requires to be set aside.

13. However, the impugned judgment and order of sentence insofar as it relates to convicting the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 323 and 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC, the evidence of the victim clearly establishes that the accused had abducted her and nothing was elicited in her cross-examination to disbelieve the same.

With regard to abduction, the testimony of the victim right from lodging of the FIR till she was subjected to cross-examination is consistent and there are no omissions and contradictions in the said statement.
Hence, the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused insofar as it relates to the offences punishable under Sections 363, 323 and 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the impugned judgment insofar as NC: 2023:KHC-K:1412 it relates to convicting the appellants-accused for the aforesaid offences does not warrant any interference.

14. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 05.05.2018 passed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge at Raichur, in S.C.No.05/2015,
insofar as it relates to convicting and sentencing the appellants-accused to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and pay fine of Rs.25,000/- each and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for one year for the offence punishable under Section 376(D) R/w Section 34 of IPC is hereby set aside and the appellants-accused are acquitted of the aforesaid offence.

2023:KHC-K:1412 sentencing the appellants-accused to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- each and in default of payment of fine shall undergo simple imprisonment for 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 323 R/w Section 34 of IPC; convicting and sentencing the appellants-accused to pay a fine of Rs.3,000/- each and in default of payment of fine shall undergo simple imprisonment for three months for the offence punishable under Section 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC

, is hereby confirmed and the appellants- accused having served the sentence imposed for the aforesaid offences, since they are in judicial custody, are directed to be released forthwith, subject to payment of fine.
iv. The Jail Authority concerned is directed to release the appellants-accused forthwith, if they are not required in any other case.
v. Office is directed to communicate the operative portion of the order to the concerned Jail Authority immediately for necessary action.
